# Independent audit: sharp hyperplane concentration from sampled superlevels



## 1. The finite lattice-volume inequality

Every finite full-rank lattice set admits a triangulation using all its points as vertices, including interior and boundary points: successive stellar subdivisions insert the additional points into the faces and stars containing them. All resulting full simplices have lattice edge determinants of nonzero integer magnitude, so each has volume at least v/r!.

The full-dimensional dual graph is connected. A generic polygonal path in the interior of the convex polytope avoids faces of codimension at least two and crosses facets, giving the required adjacency path. A spanning-tree order starts with r+1 vertices and adds at most one new vertex per full simplex, since each new simplex shares an r-vertex facet with its parent. Every triangulation vertex belongs to a full simplex. Thus t full simplices account for at most r+t vertices, proving

    vol_r(conv A)>=(|A|-r)v/r!.

The reasoning includes r=1, where simplices are intervals, facets are endpoints, and the count is exactly the usual consecutive interval count. The lattice coset translation cancels from every edge determinant.

## 2. One greedy hyperplane and the correct common threshold

For full-rank positive sampled support, greedily choosing r affinely independent points in nonincreasing value order gives an (r-1)-dimensional hyperplane E. Every point outside the final E was outside every earlier selected affine span; hence all r selected values are at least the largest outside value b>0.

For 0<t<b, the strict superlevel sample A_t contains those r points and an outside point attaining b, so it has full rank. Its finite convex hull lies in the strict superlevel by quasiconcavity, without requiring closedness or upper semicontinuity of the general function. Layer cake and the finite lattice-volume inequality yield

    M>=(v/r!)[sum_p min(f(p),b)-rb].

The selected points cancel the rb term, every outside value is at most b and is retained in full, and all remaining terms are nonnegative. This proves the exact outside-mass bound r!M/v. Ties at b are handled correctly by integrating strict levels: the integral is min(f(p),b).

If the positive sampled support has rank less than r, its integer difference span has a nonzero rational, hence integral, annihilator in lattice coordinates. The corresponding translated lattice hyperplane contains all positive samples, giving zero outside mass. Its lattice section has rank r-1 and can be spanned by r affinely independent lattice points if needed. Thus this case is not an unproved greedy termination exception.

Compact support makes the sampled positive support finite. Bounded measurability suffices for layer cake. In particular M may vanish: then a full-rank positive sampled support would contradict the same level-volume estimate, so the rank-deficient branch captures every positive sample.

## 3. Section-volume specialization and sharpness

For a compact convex Q, its s-dimensional section volumes are bounded, have compact support, and are upper semicontinuous. Compact-neighborhood containment of sections and convex-body volume continuity also handle degenerate section limits. Brunn--Minkowski gives the required convex positive superlevels. Applying the theorem to a closed cut is legitimate, but the resulting hyperplane may depend on the cut; no shared hyperplane is inferred.

At s=0 the indicator of a compact convex set supplies the same counting statement without any zero-degree root. A unimodular r-simplex times an s-body of volume V has exactly r+1 sampled bases, all positive with value V, and M=vV/r!. Every hyperplane misses at least one of the affinely independent vertices, and a facet hyperplane misses exactly one. Thus the best outside mass is V=r!M/v. This proves sharpness in the fully dimensional positive-fiber class for every r and s>=1, and in the counting case as well.

## 4. Exact retained source and smaller integer rank

Retain the ENTIRE original positive sampled fibers over E. Their base affine hull E' has rank r'<=r-1. A lattice point in the convex hull of their bases has a full s-dimensional Minkowski combination of positive source fibers inside the original Q fiber. It is therefore itself a positive sampled base on E, so its entire original fiber was retained. The convex hull of the retained fibers is contained in Q and contains all these full original fibers. Both inclusions prove exact fiber identities and exclude extra zero-mass or unsampled integer bases.

The retained body is full-dimensional in E' times R^s: its bases span E', and a full s-dimensional fiber supplies all continuous directions. The difference lattice in E' is saturated relative to L. Choosing its lattice basis changes only base coordinates and leaves all continuous H_s section measures unchanged. There is no total-dimensional determinant substituted for the fiber measure.

A containing original halfspace restricts to a containing relative halfspace or the entire retained source. The ordinary unnormalized mass comparison therefore includes every oblique direction. Conditional OC at ranks up to r-1 gives the stated retained-depth bound; using 2^(-(r-1)) instead of the actual 2^(-r') only weakens it. The retained mass fraction is at least (1-r!M/(vT))_+. For r=1, E is the greedy largest sampled point and ordinary continuous Grünbaum is the only input.

## 5. Bounded coarse-level consequence

On each coarse level with positive fine mass, the theorem gives a retained hyperplane source. Their retained masses sum to at least T-r!M/v; coarse levels without positive fine mass add only nonnegative coarse volume and do not invalidate this lower bound. Averaging over J nonempty coarse levels selects one retained source of mass at least (T-r!M/v)_+/J.

The smaller-rank theorem is applied only inside that selected level, whose exact lattice-source reduction was just proved. Every containing cap of the original larger source retains at least this selected source mass. Hence the stated depth bound and the sufficient conditions J<=2^k and M/(vT)<=1/(2r!) follow. The common covolume v cancels from the fine normalized mass. Different levelwise hyperplanes do not need to form a globally compatible new body because only one level is selected.

No parity bound on J, arbitrary-level allocation, or feasible rounding is silently assumed. All those restrictions remain explicit. No defect was found in the exact concentration theorem or its conditional corollaries.
